seoTitle: How to Create an Instagram Reel in Canva
metaDescription: Build an Instagram Reel from a Canva template: rewrite the text, swap the audio from the Audio tab, then download as MP4 or post straight to Instagram. Includes the Free plan's 1080p export limit.
intro:
Canva's Reels templates arrive with the animation, timing and vertical format already done. Your job is mostly editorial: replace the placeholder words, check the music still fits, and get the file out.

This guide follows that route from template search to posting. It also covers the parts that trip people up at the end. Canva Free locks the export quality at the default 1080p. Premium elements and tracks trigger a payment prompt. And audio you upload yourself can block publishing if Canva's copyright check flags it.
costNote: A Reel can be made and downloaded on Canva Free. Free accounts export MP4 at the default 1080p (up to 30 minutes long); choosing 480p, 720p or 4K brings up an upgrade prompt. Templates or tracks marked with a Pro icon or a price need Canva Pro or a one-off purchase at download time, and a purchased premium track covers one design only.

steps.heading: Search the templates for Instagram Reels
steps.body:
Open the Templates panel and search "instagram reels". The results are already the vertical Reels size, and the Category, Style and Language filters above the grid help narrow them. Each thumbnail plays a short animated preview.

Judge the motion, not just the layout. A template whose cuts feel too slow or frantic in a two-second preview will feel the same once your words are in it. Check for a Pro icon or price tag too, since those elements have to be paid for when you download.

image.caption: Canva's Templates panel filtered to "instagram reels," showing a grid of vertical video templates with play previews.

steps.heading: Open the template and watch it through once
steps.body:
The example here is a "Blue Modern Marketing Tips Instagram Reel". It loads with a scrubbable timeline along the bottom and a Preview button above the editor. It runs 42 seconds: cartoon character animation, a text card reading "Feeling Lost in Marketing? Use the customer's journey map to navigate the way," and handle and website text underneath.

Play it end to end before changing anything. You'll see which parts are structure you want to keep and which lines have to become yours.

image.caption: A marketing-tips Reel template open in the editor, with its animation preview and a full timeline strip along the bottom.

steps.heading: Rewrite the text, including every repeated handle
steps.body:
Expanding the timeline shows each text element as its own bar, so you can see when the headline, the handle (@reallygreatsite) and the website URL appear across the 42 seconds. Select a text element and type over it. Here "Feeling Lost in Marketing?" became "Feeling Lost in Technology?" with the layout and animation timing untouched.

Then hunt down the small stuff. Templates repeat the placeholder handle and reallygreatsite.com at the bottom of several frames, and they're easy to miss because the headline draws the eye. Scrub the whole timeline and replace every instance with your real handle or link.

image.caption: The Reel's timeline expanded to show individual text segments, with the headline text already rewritten for a new topic.

steps.heading: Tighten the pacing and swap the audio
steps.body:
Scrub through once more and look for any card that holds a beat too long. Reels lose viewers quickly, so trim it. The entrance and exit animations stay attached to each element, so shortening a section doesn't mean rebuilding it.

Music is added from the Audio tab in the editor's side panel. If you don't see that tab, open Apps first, or go to Elements and choose Audio. Clicking a track drops it in at the playhead's position on the timeline. To remove the template's original track, right-click its coloured bar below the page thumbnails and choose Delete track, or select it and use Volume to mute it. You can also upload your own music, but Canva runs an audio fingerprint check on uploads. If a track infringes copyright, you won't be able to publish the design with that audio.

steps.heading: Download the MP4 or post it to Instagram
steps.body:
Click Share, then Download, and pick MP4 Video as the file type. On Canva Free leave Quality at the default: changing it to 480p, 720p or 4K shows an upgrade prompt. Canva says that prompt is not a download error. Paid plans can go up to 4K on desktop. The file keeps the Reels format, so you can post it through Instagram's own app with no resizing.

To skip the download, click Share, then See all, and choose Instagram. The first time, Canva asks you to connect and log in to the account. After that you can publish from the editor or schedule the Reel in Canva's Content Planner. If you used paid music, verify its licence when downloading so the post doesn't pick up a copyright claim.

troubleshooting.problem: An upgrade prompt appears when you try to download
troubleshooting.cause: On Canva Free, changing MP4 quality from the default (including picking 480p, 720p or 4K) triggers an upgrade prompt.
troubleshooting.fix: Set Quality back to the default and download again. Free exports at 1080p, which is fine for Reels.

troubleshooting.problem: The Download button reads Pay and download
troubleshooting.cause: The template or a track in it is a Pro or paid element.
troubleshooting.fix: Pay for the element, upgrade, or replace the flagged item with a free one before downloading.

troubleshooting.problem: Canva won't publish the Reel with your uploaded song
troubleshooting.cause: Canva fingerprints uploaded music. If the track infringes copyright, the design can't be published with that audio.
troubleshooting.fix: Replace it with a track from Canva's Audio tab or music you hold the rights to.

faq.question: Do I need video editing experience to make a Reel in Canva?
faq.answer: No. A Reels template already has its animation and pacing built in, so most of the work is rewriting the text and deciding whether the music fits.

faq.question: Can I post the Reel from Canva without downloading it?
faq.answer: Yes. Go to Share, then See all, then Instagram, and connect your account the first time. Instagram designs can also be scheduled from Canva's Content Planner.

faq.question: Can I export the Reel in 4K for free?
faq.answer: No. Canva Free downloads MP4 at the default 1080p. 4K is available on paid plans and only on desktop.

faq.question: How do I replace the template's music?
faq.answer: Delete or mute the existing track from the timeline, then add a new one from the Audio tab in the side panel. It lands wherever the playhead sits.

faq.question: Can I reuse the same template for a series of Reels?
faq.answer: Yes. Duplicate the finished design and change the text and media for each new Reel. Note that a premium track bought on Canva Free covers only one design, so reusing it in a copy means buying it again.
